name: Terminal Pet
tag: A little company while Claude works.
does: Adds a pixel crab above the prompt. It reacts when Claude reads, writes, waits, finishes, or hits an error. Its belly reflects conversation fullness.
use: Start with /pet on, then /pet party for an instant preview. Ask Claude to read the demo files to see real activity.
cmd:
/pet on
/pet name Pixel
/pet party
/pet wake
/pet off
prompt: Read README.md and src/auth/login.ts. Explain what the demo does in two short sentences.
nl: Use the slash commands. This mod does not register a plain-English control tool.
limit: A mood is decoration. A nervous pet does not stop a dangerous action. Feed and party are preview controls, not real usage readings.
spec: Draw a pixel crab above the prompt with distinct idle, reading, writing, working, waiting, error, sleeping and celebration states. Use original pixel art. Animate terminal raster and desktop SVG separately within host limits. Reflect measured context fullness in the belly; label forced preview states. Support name, on, off, sleep, wake, party and feed controls. Keep permission surveys visible. Persist preferences and stop needless redraws when hidden.
tests: Test every sprite size, color budget, mood transition, hide/show, narrow layouts, desktop SVG limits and permission-survey precedence.

name: Coral Skin
tag: Make the work easier to scan.
does: Changes supported Claude Code message and tool rows to a coral, ink and cream style. Colored chips help you spot reads, edits and commands.
use: Run /skin on, then ask Claude to inspect the demo. Run /skin off to compare.
prompt: Read README.md, inspect src/auth/login.ts, and explain the login flow without editing anything.
nl: Use /skin. Asking for a color in normal chat does not reliably change this mod.
limit: Risk colors are visual hints, not security checks. This is Coral Skin; the separate Crimson Garden theme shown elsewhere is not bundled.
spec: Style supported message, tool, spinner and footer components in coral, ink and cream. Show readable type-specific chips for reads, edits and shell commands. Keep original permission controls and tool results intact. Provide /skin on, off and risk. Off must restore normal rendering, including already mounted rows. Expose named palette constants so a beginner can ask to change the palette.
tests: Test terminal and desktop component output, runtime toggling, risk-chip grouping, readable contrast and preservation of original permission UI.

name: Context Meter
tag: See how full the conversation is.
does: Shows conversation fullness, session cost and available usage-limit readings above the prompt. Think of it as a dashboard gauge.
use: It appears automatically after loading. Send a normal message and wait for a measurement. There is no /context-meter command.
prompt: Read README.md and explain this project in plain English.
off: Disable the plugin and start a fresh session.
nl: Automatic. No special prompt is needed.
limit: A full conversation is not an intelligence score. Dollars are API-equivalent usage, not a charge against your subscription. Missing usage data may be unavailable, not zero.
spec: Render a compact AbovePrompt gauge using actual session context, cost and rate-limit data. Label percent fullness, token use, session cost and available five-hour/weekly limits. Handle missing data honestly. Respond to session measurement events. Yield to permission surveys. Keep it legible on narrow terminals and desktop. Do not invent a cost estimate when the host does not provide one.
tests: Test changing measurements, missing or zero values, narrow rendering and permission surveys. Use no model call to draw the meter.

name: Repo Heatmap
does: Draws a map of files in the current project. File areas reflect size, and colors react to reads, searches, edits and failed operations.
use: In the demo project, open /heatmap before sending the prompt. Watch files light up while Claude works.
cmd:
/heatmap open
/heatmap size lines
/heatmap rescan
/heatmap reset
/heatmap close
prompt: Investigate the login flow, from src/ui/LoginForm.tsx through src/auth/login.ts, session.ts and tokens.ts. Read the files and explain how a user gets signed in. Do not edit anything.
nl: Open it with /heatmap. The investigation itself is a normal English prompt.
limit: Tracks activity observed during this session. A bright file is not proof of importance or a bug. Some shell activity is inferred and may not map perfectly.
spec: Scan the working project and draw a squarified treemap with file area by bytes or lines. Observe direct file tools and recognizable shell/search results, distinguishing reads, edits and failures. Animate touches, then settle to a visited tint. Ignore generated and hidden bulk. Cap rendering work for large projects. Provide open, close, reset, rescan and size commands. Explain an empty or too-narrow pane.
tests: Test nonoverlap and proportional areas, path normalization, search hits, failure classification, bounded color count, animation decay and terminal/desktop rendering.

name: Flight Recorder
tag: See the work unfold on a timeline.
does: Shows turns, tool activity and helper activity over time so you can see when work happened and what ran alongside it.
use: Run /timeline open, then ask for two read-only helper investigations. Helpers appear only if Claude actually starts them.
prompt: Use two read-only helper agents: one to inspect the login flow, and one to inspect configuration and tests. Wait for both, then give me a short combined summary. Do not edit files.
nl: Use /timeline to open it. Request helper work in plain English.
limit: A timeline is a record of observed events, not proof that parallel work was faster. Cost figures use a static estimate and can differ from billing, including cache-write charges.
spec: Build a timeline pane for main turns, tool spans and named helper lanes. Track starts and completions, label failures and elapsed times, and keep bounded history. Do not count background notifications as fresh human tasks. Support open, close, clear and turns. Preserve the underlying work. If costs are shown, label them estimates and show missing model prices as unknown.
tests: Test overlapping helpers, parent/child events, incomplete spans, notification filtering, bounded history and both UI surfaces. Do not claim a speedup or cost saving from fixture data.

name: Model Router
tag: Choose a lighter model for helper work.
does: Routes supported helper-agent steps to Sonnet by default while the main conversation keeps its own model. Haiku is an option.
use: Check /router, choose subagents mode, then request a helper. A route only happens if the pricing table knows the original model and considers the target cheaper.
prompt: Use the Explore agent to find where the port is configured in this folder and what reads config/config.json, then tell me in two sentences. Do not edit files.
nl: Controls use /router. Ask Claude to use a helper in a normal prompt.
limit: Changes which model does real work. Review the answer. Model availability and prices can change; unknown models may stay unchanged. Savings are estimates, not a quality guarantee. Experimental steps/both modes can lose cache benefits.
spec: Default to routing only helper-agent steps to Sonnet, with Haiku selectable. Keep every main-conversation step on its own model in this mode. Treat both undefined and null agent IDs as the main conversation. Route only known more-expensive models. Keep unknown models unchanged. Support on, off, status and explicit experimental steps/both modes. Persist preferences. Report decisions and clearly labeled price-table estimates without guaranteeing savings or quality.
tests: Test null/undefined main IDs, actual helper IDs, cheaper and unknown source models, disabled mode, model settings and cold/warm-cache accounting. Never invent model IDs or prices; inspect current supported ones.

name: Output Tray
tag: Find the files Claude just made.
does: Collects new files created during the session in a panel with copy, open and reveal actions.
use: Run /tray show, send the file-creation prompt, then /tray list. This starter kit implements Open and Reveal using macOS Finder.
cmd:
/tray show
/tray list
/tray open 1
/tray reveal 1
/tray copy 1
/tray close
prompt: Create demo-output if it does not exist. Write a short explanation of this demo project to demo-output/project-overview.md and a file inventory to demo-output/file-inventory.csv. Use a new numbered filename if either exists. Use the Write tool for each file. Do not edit existing files.
nl: “Open the output tray” or “List the files in the output tray” is supported by a registered tool. The model cannot use that tool to launch files.
limit: Lists newly created files, not every edited file. Start tracking before the work. Clear removes the list, not the files. Mac Open/Reveal is not a cross-platform file opener.
spec: Track new files created by direct Write, notebook edits, shell commands and turn-boundary snapshots. Ignore failed, denied or staged-only writes. Deduplicate paths and flag missing files. Provide a list pane, number selection, copy path, explicit Open and Reveal. Scripts must open as text and apps/executables must only be revealed. Never execute a file automatically. Let the model show/list the tray but never open a file. Handle null main-agent IDs.
tests: Test direct and shell creation, existing files, denial, deletion, spaced paths, helper tags, null turn boundaries, narrow-pane fallback and exact user-only open arguments.

name: Changes Receipt
tag: Get a clear list of what changed.
does: Summarizes files created, edited and deleted during a tracked turn. It separates successful changes from failed attempts.
use: Run /receipt on before the file-creation prompt. Wait until Claude finishes, then run /receipt last.
prompt: Create demo-output if needed. Use the Write tool to create demo-output/receipt-example.md with three bullet points about the login flow. If that filename exists, create a new numbered filename. Do not modify any other file.
nl: “Show the changes receipt” is supported. Slash commands are the clearest way to check the last tracked turn.
limit: A receipt is not undo, backup or perfect attribution. Other programs changing files at the same time can confuse snapshots. It does not backfill old sessions.
spec: Snapshot the project at main-turn boundaries and combine Git changes or a filesystem fallback with direct tool evidence. Report creates, changes, deletions, renames and failed attempts separately. Preserve writes from the main turn when helpers start and finish. Accept null main-agent IDs. Provide on, off, open, close, last and bounded history. Add a natural-language tool that reads receipts. Do not imply rollback.
tests: Test dirty files before a turn, changes to dirty files, failed and denied writes, shell renames, non-Git projects, outside paths, helper interleaving, missing turn-start evidence and both UI surfaces.

name: Session Bookmarks
tag: Leave yourself a useful “come back here” note.
does: Saves a title and a short note with the project and session reference, so you can find the conversation again.
use: Run /bm save Login walkthrough; next run /bm list. Use /bm resume 1 and paste the copied command into a new terminal.
cmd:
/bm save Login walkthrough
/bm list
/bm find login
/bm open
/bm resume 1
/bm close
prompt: Bookmark this session as “Login walkthrough” with the note “Read the auth files; next step is writing a plain-English overview.”
nl: “Bookmark this session” and “Find my bookmark about login” are supported.
limit: Resume copies a terminal command; it does not switch your current desktop chat. The folder and original transcript must still exist. A blank /bm uses a short model call to suggest a title; an explicit note avoids that call.
spec: Save only explicit bookmarks with title, note, project, branch, working folder, session ID, transcript path and timestamps. Store a user-local JSON file with restrictive permissions and atomic writes. Do not copy transcripts. Allow explicit notes without model calls; optional automatic titles use a bounded call with fallback. Implement list, search, rename, delete, panel and resume. Resume must safely quote the folder and copy/print a command, never claim in-chat switching.
tests: Test persistence, corrupt-file backup, missing folders, quoted paths, explicit-note no-call behavior, title failure fallback, confirm-before-delete in the pane and both UI surfaces.

name: Auto Handoff
tag: Leave the next chat a useful starting point.
does: Writes a summary of progress, decisions and next steps into the project so a fresh conversation can continue with that summary.
use: After a short task, run /autohandoff now. Read the generated handoff before trusting it. In a fresh session in the same folder, ask Claude to read handoff/LATEST.md.
prompt: Read handoff/LATEST.md, follow its link to the handoff file, and summarize the next step. Do not change anything until I choose a task.
nl: The save controls use /autohandoff. Reading the handoff in the next chat is a normal prompt.
limit: Summaries can miss details and use an extra model call. The default automatic threshold is 85%. Files remain in your project after disabling; review them before sharing. It does not automatically create a new chat.
spec: At a configurable context threshold, request a concise handoff summary and write a timestamped Markdown file plus LATEST.md. Include goals, completed work, decisions, touched files, checks and next actions; tell the summarizer to exclude secrets. Preserve existing project pointers and add handoff to Git ignore without rewriting unrelated entries. Provide status, now, resume, threshold, on and off. Do not overwrite a good handoff with an empty reply. Resume validates the target before submitting a prompt.
tests: Test threshold crossing/rearming, before-compaction behavior, failed-save retry, empty-summary protection, missing-target resume, file names, ignore preservation and extra-model-call boundaries.
